claim: Heatmap 'Balanced' sizing gives tiles a minimum area (1,400 px2; 2,200 grouped); 0 undersized tiles at 360-1280 px, 2 at 320 px grouped. True market cap sizing stays literal.
so_what: Accepted trade-off at 320 px.

claim: 18 single-colour coin logos (6 white, 12 black) were invisible or near-invisible on one theme family; flipped by theme tokens since PR #15.
so_what: New logos: run node scripts/build-coin-icons.mjs --tones; seo-lint fails if a mark is missing.

claim: axe-core: 0 violations on 16 page types x dark and light themes; nothing below 12 px; touch targets at least 38 px on phones; dialogs keep focus inside (page behind is inert).
so_what: Run bash tests/run.sh after any UI change; it includes axe.

claim: GPT-5.3 Instant (Mar 2026) and later ChatGPT models link out less and run more sub-queries, including checks for third-party validation; studies conflict on whether backlinks or outbound links affect citations.
so_what: Third-party mentions (GitHub, launch posts, data posts others cite) matter more than on-page tricks.

claim: Google's guide to generative AI features: 'optimizing for generative AI search is still SEO'; no special markup or llms.txt needed (llms.txt note added June 2026); value non-commodity content; update dates only when content changes; spam policies apply to AI responses.
so_what: Matches our approach (computed, dated, unique facts; honest lastmod). Keep llms.txt only because it costs nothing for other tools.

claim: Search Console Settings has a 'Search generative AI' control (default Include) deciding eligibility for AI Overviews and AI Mode; rolled out from the UK to other countries during 2026.
so_what: Owner: confirm it says Include once the property is verified.

claim: AI Mode and AI Overviews add more inline links, 'official websites' sections and news carousels (Google blog, Oct 15).
so_what: Clicks from AI answers favour pages that do what an answer can't: live, interactive data. Supports the live-product and citable-facts pillars.

claim: Ahrefs tracked 37,500 AI citations over 20 days: citations churn day to day; for Google AI Overviews/AI Mode ranking at all matters more than position; pages cited by AI were on average 25.7% fresher than organic results, and a refreshed data page gained citations within days.
so_what: Real data updates (weekly stats, dated key facts) are the right freshness lever; changing dates without content has no evidence and breaks our lastmod rule.

claim: Google, Microsoft (Bing), OpenAI and Anthropic back one robots.txt AI-training opt-out from the IETF AIPREF draft ('user-agent: __usage_ai-training'). Google will read an opt-out as disallowing Google-Extended (not Search) and plans support in early 2027; Bing applies its training/grounding preferences from Feb 1, 2027.
so_what: Owner chose to welcome AI training crawlers: add nothing. Revisit when the token is final (2027).

claim: AI Overviews show on over 80% of Google searches (Search Engine Roundtable, third-party data); one opt-out study puts AI Overview/AI Mode click-through at about 0.9%.
so_what: Expect few clicks from informational queries; the site's draw is the live product (alerts, heatmap, widgets) and citable dated facts.

claim: OAI-SearchBot decides inclusion in ChatGPT search; GPTBot is training only; ChatGPT-User fetches on a user's request. ChatGPT search leans on Bing's index plus OpenAI's own crawl.
so_what: All three are allowed in robots.txt; IndexNow to Bing helps ChatGPT discovery indirectly.

claim: OpenAI launched 'Businesses in ChatGPT' (beta, Nov 10): claim or create a profile at chatgpt.com/business-hub, verify the domain with a DNS TXT record and your identity (Persona), pick a category and description. Online-only businesses are eligible (unlike Google Business Profile). Insights show mentions (ChatGPT referencing your website) and website clicks; claiming doesn't guarantee placement.
so_what: The first source of ChatGPT mention and click counts for this site. Owner decision: it needs the owner's identity verification and a DNS record. Description: plain words people use ('live crypto prices from Coinbase, Binance and Kraken').

claim: Gemini 4 Hydrogen became the default model in Google AI Mode for everyone on Nov 12 and answers the 'hardest' AI Overview questions; Google says it fans out queries more widely and links a broader range of sites (no numbers).
so_what: AI Mode/AI Overview citation data for November spans this model change (Nov 12) and the core update (Nov 10); compare before/after each date separately.

claim: Google is testing removing the AI Mode button from the search bar and 'Ask anything' (unconfirmed test).
so_what: Nothing to do; affects how many people reach AI Mode.

claim: Yahoo Scout will pay publishers through the ILC for using content in AI answers.
so_what: Not relevant at our size; watch if licensing programmes open to small data sites.

claim: Large publishers plan for less search traffic: Ziff Davis reported organic Google referrals down about 37% year over year (Q3 2026) and is 'not planning on a search recovery'; Tripadvisor expects SEO to weigh on 2027.
so_what: Growth should not depend on Google clicks alone: alerts, widgets (embeds on other sites), the installable app and direct visits matter.

claim: AI assistants cite different sources: Ahrefs found 86% of top-mentioned sources are not shared across ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Overviews; Perplexity cites the most sources per answer, Claude the fewest (vendor studies, uncontrolled).
so_what: No single 'AI SEO' target. Be crawlable by every AI crawler and keep facts dated and specific.

claim: Claude's web search results overlap strongly with Brave Search's top results (13 of 15 in one test); Brave is on Anthropic's subprocessor list since March 2025.
so_what: Being indexed by Brave (it crawls on its own; no submission tool) helps visibility in Claude answers. ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User are allowed.

claim: Bing Webmaster Tools AI Performance report (preview since Feb 2026): Copilot/Bing AI citations, cited pages, grounding queries; June 2026 added Intents, Topics, Citation Share and Compare; Oct 13 added Topics Portfolio. No click data.
so_what: Owner: import the site from Search Console into Bing Webmaster Tools; read AI Performance monthly.

claim: Bing announced separate AI Training and page-level AI Grounding preferences (Disallow / DisallowExtended), honoured from 1 Feb 2027; they replace NoArchive/NoCache for these uses. Disallowing grounding reduces visibility in Bing AI Mode, AI Overview and Copilot; Bing search eligibility is unchanged.
so_what: Default (allowed) is what we want: set nothing. Re-check the exact syntax before Feb 2027 in case the default changes.

claim: Microsoft retired the 'Copilot Search' name: Bing's AI surfaces are now 'AI Mode' and 'AI Overview'.
so_what: Use these names when reading Bing reports.

claim: Bing documented an AI-off option: a preview Chrome/Edge extension (also makes Bing the default engine) and the '-ai' query operator, which remove AI answers from Bing results.
so_what: Nothing to do; a small share of Bing users will see classic results only.

claim: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5): 1M context, 128K output, thinking always on, default effort medium, knowledge cutoff June 2026; $4/$20 per MTok per Anthropic's platform docs (one Anthropic page lists $8/$40; check before quoting).
so_what: Default effort medium for routine work; high/xhigh for audits, redesigns and hard bugs.

claim: Anthropic donated the Agent Skills standard (SKILL.md) to the Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation); skills stay portable across tools.
so_what: Keep repeated workflows as skills in .claude/skills/ (ship exists); a 'kb' or 'research' skill could follow.

claim: Claude Code 2.1.311: typing 'ultrathink' runs that turn at xhigh effort on the newest models (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ULTRATHINK turns the keyword off).
so_what: Use 'ultrathink' for a single hard turn instead of raising the whole session's effort.

claim: Fast mode on Opus 4.8 is deprecated and removed on Nov 30, 2026 (requests then error); migrate to Opus 5.5 for the speedup.
so_what: No effect here (sessions use Opus 5.5).

claim: Claude Code 2.1.316-2.1.317: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT sets the effort subagents run at; subagents on a different model use that model's saved effort; a subagent's frontmatter 'effort:' wins.
so_what: For fan-out research or audits, run subagents at low/medium and keep the main session at medium.

claim: Claude Code 2.1.317 removed the Read tool's 'file unchanged since your last Read' stub: reading an unchanged file again returns its full content (and costs tokens again).
so_what: Don't re-read large files; use grep or read line ranges (CLAUDE.md 'keep sessions cheap').

claim: Scheduled tasks: saved prompt + repositories + connectors on Anthropic's cloud; choose model and effort; no more often than hourly; runs push claude/-prefixed branches and need the repository attached.
so_what: Two daily tasks replace the weekly one (switched off 12 Nov): CPT daily build (Sonnet) needs usaflees/cpt attached; CPT daily check (Haiku) runs. Prompts: docs/DAILY-TASKS.md.

claim: Anthropic's top Claude Code practice: give Claude a check it can run; rules that must never break belong in hooks, CI or tests, not prose; keep CLAUDE.md short (under about 200 lines).
so_what: bash tests/run.sh is the gate; seo-lint and kb.mjs --check enforce rules; CLAUDE.md stays short.

claim: A scheduled task includes every connected claude.ai connector by default and can use them during a run, including writes; claude.ai custom connectors also reach Claude Code cloud sessions.
so_what: Keep scheduled tasks for this repo connector-free (both daily tasks have none); add a connector only for a named need.

claim: A research subagent stopped at the 5-hour usage limit keeps the notes it already wrote; the task notification says it can be resumed with SendMessage after the reset instead of starting over.
so_what: Have research subagents write notes to files as they go; resume rather than re-spawn.

claim: Three deep-research runs (5, 5 and 3 parallel subagents plus a report writer) used about 3.3 million tokens in one chat; each long chat also re-reads its whole history on every message.
so_what: Deep research only for decisions that need it; start a fresh chat per topic; put routine work in docs/QUEUE.md.

claim: Seven parallel chats on this repo re-merged and re-tested each other's work and hit the usage limit repeatedly.
so_what: One chat at a time; routine work goes through docs/QUEUE.md and the daily tasks.

claim: Measured run costs: CPT daily check on Haiku 5.5 about $0.006 per run (40 live checks); CPT daily build on Sonnet 5.5 about $0.07 when it stops at its access test.
so_what: Health checks belong on Haiku; build work on Sonnet; Opus/Fable only in interactive chats that need them.

claim: In a scheduled cloud run without the repository attached, anonymous curl calls to api.github.com (Actions runs, open pull requests) were refused with 403, so the daily check reported CI as unknown.
so_what: Attach usaflees/cpt to the daily check too, or have it read CI through git instead of the REST API.

claim: Running local QA then preview QA in a row exceeded Kraken's per-IP WebSocket limit (HTTP 429) when every crawled page connected.
so_what: The crawl now opens real Kraken sockets on 12 sampled pages only.

claim: Fresh-news research works best with several 'extended' web searches in one turn, then fetching the primary pages (Search Central 'What's new', Search Status Dashboard, platform blogs) to confirm what trade press reports.
so_what: Record each finding here with its date, confidence and sources; prefer 'official' over 'reported' over 'claim'.

claim: Right after tests/wait-deploy.sh reported a branch preview as deployed, Cloudflare Pages answered HTTP 500 for every URL for a short time (check-live: 43 problems); a minute later the same checks passed 39/39 and the crawl of 136 pages was clean.
so_what: If check-live fails on every URL with 500 just after a deploy, re-run it once before investigating; a second failure is real.

claim: scripts/seo-audit.mjs reads every sitemap page as crawlers do and reports words, own-phrase share per template, title/H1/description agreement, heading order, alt text, link text, inbound links, OG/Twitter tags, JSON-LD fields, stray template text and brand facts. 16 Nov baseline: coin pages avg 762 words, 47% own phrases; sector pages 303 words, 55%; 5 pages under 250 words (heatmap, race, privacy and gaming sectors, one more). 17 Nov: 0 findings; sector pages avg 984 words, 64% own phrases.
so_what: Run it before and after any SEO pass and compare; seo-lint stays the gate.

claim: Cloudflare Crawler Hints sends change signals to IndexNow engines; a Cloudflare-OpenAI pilot (since July, ~1% of the network) also feeds new-page and change signals, metadata only, to OpenAI's search crawler.
so_what: Owner toggle in Cloudflare (Caching > Configuration > Crawler Hints). Complements our CI IndexNow job and may reach ChatGPT search, which doesn't use IndexNow.

claim: Cloudflare's CEO said OpenAI pays Cloudflare for hints telling its crawler when pages change (pilot since July 2026); over half of AI crawler fetches re-fetch unchanged pages. Cloudflare's Crawler Hints (all plans) also send IndexNow signals inferred from cache changes.
so_what: Owner: Cloudflare -> Caching -> Configuration -> Crawler Hints: On. Our own IndexNow job stays (it's exact); honest lastmod matters more now.

claim: Cloudflare can serve text/markdown to agents that ask for it (zone setting, AI Crawl Control); no code needed.
so_what: Owner may switch it on; low priority.

claim: The zone's default Browser Cache TTL overrides our headers for some files (robots.txt served with 4 h max-age).
so_what: Owner: Caching -> Browser Cache TTL -> 'Respect Existing Headers'.

claim: AI Crawl Control is on every Cloudflare plan (allow/block/charge per AI crawler); Pay per crawl is moving toward paying for value (citations) rather than fetches.
so_what: Owner chose to welcome AI crawlers: make sure no Cloudflare bot setting blocks or challenges them (check-live verifies search and AI crawlers aren't blocked).

claim: Crypto prices are YMYL; Google's scaled-content abuse policy targets large sets of templated pages with little unique value. Mueller (Sep 2026): low-value programmatic pages can hold a whole site back for a long time.
so_what: Every coin page carries computed, dated facts nobody else phrases the same way; no per-currency or prediction pages; hold new URL families until half the current pages are indexed.

claim: Google's 'using generative AI content' guide (Oct 1) adds rater-guideline material: fact-check AI-assisted text including titles, descriptions, structured data and alt text; no invented authors.
so_what: Our page text is computed from data or reviewed (coin-about.json); titles come from templates. Keep 'no AI filler' and human review of coin-about.json.

claim: AI-written filler, near-duplicate page families (price in every currency, price predictions), fake authors and reviews are spam-policy risks; Anthropic's usage policy (effective Nov 12, 2026) bars using Claude to seed manipulative content for AI answers.
so_what: Don't build them; DECISIONS forbids FAQ/Product/Dataset markup, per-currency and prediction pages.

claim: Google drops fast-changing prices from title links and rewrites titles it considers inaccurate; it keeps the page's own title about 87% of the time by its count (independent studies: 33-76% rewritten).
so_what: Titles at most 60 characters, no live prices or dates; descriptions at most 160 (seo-lint enforces). Write for people, then leave them alone.

claim: AI fetchers and many crawlers skip JavaScript, so the first screen must carry real, dated numbers.
so_what: Coin pages open with a dated key-facts line (close, 1-year change, distance from high, rank).

claim: Per-page unique, verifiable data is the defence against scaled-content risk: performance stats, monthly closes, best/worst month, largest fall, 90-day BTC correlation, sector rank, per-exchange prices.
so_what: Keep adding computed facts, never written filler. Next: all-time-high/drawdown once a reliable ATH source exists; static spread snapshot.

claim: Late alerts top user complaints about rival price apps, ahead of ads and paywalls; rivals sell alerts, portfolio tracking, widgets, API access and ad-free use.
so_what: Free, honest alerts (price, move, portfolio, keep-alive) shipped; keep them reliable and fast.

claim: No free licence covers displaying third-party headlines: publisher RSS, Google News and free news-API tiers forbid public display; AI 'why it moved' text without citable sources would be filler.
so_what: Newsflash reports measured facts only. Headlines and AI summaries wait for a licensed feed and an owner decision.

claim: Crypto media saw large core-update swings in 2024-2026 (e.g. Cointelegraph's organic traffic fell sharply from late 2025); analysts attribute losses to weak trust signals and scaled content. No data isolates price-data sites in the Nov 2026 update.
so_what: Keep trust pages (/trust/, /about/ methodology, sources), no invented authors, no AI filler; measure after the update instead of reacting during it.

claim: AI answers are corrected by fixing the sources they ground on: plain, dated statements of current facts near the top of the pages indexed first; contradictions across pages ('new domain owner' vs same owner) read as a different entity.
so_what: Keep 'live, relaunched Oct 2026 by the original owner, privacy-first' consistent on home, /about/, /trust/, llms.txt and Organization markup; seo-audit checks the brand facts.

claim: Preferred Sources, feed readers (Chrome iOS Follow, Feedly, Inoreader) and AI crawlers favour dated content that changes on a schedule; the site's only regularly changing page content is the weekly data refresh.
so_what: Next build (queued): a weekly computed market report page with an Atom feed, built from the refresh data. Needs the owner's OK on NEWS-AND-MONETIZATION §9 (it's data, not headlines or AI text).

claim: Coin pages put the converter (about 50 identical currency/coin labels) before the unique performance figures and 'About' text.
so_what: Moved the converter below 'About' (16 Nov): crawlers and AI fetchers reading top-down reach unique figures first. #convert anchor unchanged.

claim: Static HTML under 250 visible words: /heatmap/, /race/ and the smallest sector hubs (privacy 195, gaming 233).
so_what: Done 17 Nov: sector hubs list every coin with dated figures and its 1-year rank in that hub (full sentence only on the coin's main hub, so overlapping hubs don't repeat paragraphs); /heatmap/ and /race/ carry a dated weekly-moves table. seo-audit: 0 findings.

claim: Exchange market-data terms (Coinbase 'Derived Works', OKX, Binance) restrict public display of their data, live prices included.
so_what: Owner: accept and document, license, or ask in writing before any sponsor or ads.

claim: Google uses og:image for Search and Discover thumbnails (March 2026).
so_what: Every page has its own og:image (per-coin JPEGs). Compliant.

claim: Preferred sources (users pick favourite sites) now also apply in AI Overviews and AI Mode; sites may link https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=<domain>. Usage up about 7x since January (Google, Oct 15).
so_what: The deeplink was removed 16 Nov because the tool doesn't list this site yet (see google-preferred-sources-ineligible). Aimed at news sources.

claim: 'Control what you share with Google Search' now lists robots meta, data-nosnippet, X-Robots-Tag and the Search Console 'Search generative AI' control together.
so_what: We use X-Robots-Tag for /embed/ (noindex, indexifembedded) and pages.dev; no snippet limits anywhere, which keeps AI features eligible.

claim: URL structure guidance clarified: separate words with hyphens, not underscores.
so_what: All our URLs are lower-case tickers or hyphenated slugs (/sector/layer-1/). Compliant.

claim: Search Central updated user-generated spam guidance: keep link-shared user content out of the index and watch abuse in Search Console.
so_what: No user-generated pages here (sync links put data in the URL but are never linked or indexed). Nothing to do.

claim: Favicon doc: Googlebot must reach the home page and follow its redirects; at least 48x48 px recommended.
so_what: favicon.ico carries 16/32/48 px and favicon.svg exists; robots.txt allows the home page. Compliant.

claim: Google may be bringing back the &num=100 results parameter (Search Engine Roundtable, unconfirmed).
so_what: Only matters for rank-tracking tools; nothing to do.

claim: Google's November 2026 core update started Nov 10 (10:07 PT), global, all languages; rollout may take up to 2 weeks. Third core update of 2026 (after May; spam update Sep 24-Oct 8).
so_what: Don't judge ranking or indexing changes before about a week after Google marks it complete. Log Nov 10 as an annotation in any measurement. No site change needed for the update itself.

claim: Google's Preferred Sources tool shows 'No results' for cryptopriceticker.com; it lists only regularly updated sources (domain or subdomain, included in Search generative AI features).
so_what: Removed the dead 'add us as a preferred source' links (home footer, /about/). Re-add once the tool finds the domain; a dated, regularly updated page (weekly report + feed) would help.

claim: Google does not participate in IndexNow; it discovers changes through sitemaps and links. Participants: Bing, Yandex, Seznam, Naver, Yep, Amazon, Internet Archive (one submission is shared with all).
so_what: IndexNow runs automatically after each release for Bing and others; Google needs Search Console + sitemaps.

claim: Google warns against bumping lastmod/dates to look fresh; lastmod should change only with real content changes.
so_what: Sitemap lastmod uses the data date and content hashes for hand-written pages (content/page-dates.json).

claim: Google renders a page once and indexes that snapshot; links and canonicals must be in the initial HTML; live WebSocket values are unlikely to be indexed.
so_what: Every page ships a static data snapshot (stats, monthly closes, converter tables) and plain <a href> links; canonical in the HTML.

claim: A Content-Signal line in robots.txt makes Lighthouse's validator fail ('Unknown directive', SEO 100 -> 92); RFC 9309 parsers ignore it.
so_what: Removed; seo-lint rejects anything but User-agent/Allow/Disallow/Sitemap in robots.txt.

claim: Search Console URL Inspection 'Request indexing' accepts roughly 10 URLs a day per property; repeating a request doesn't help. URL Inspection API: 2,000 inspections a day.
so_what: Owner works through the daily list in INDEXING-PLAN.md (about two weeks).

claim: Search Console Domain property is verified; sitemaps to submit: sitemap.xml plus sitemap-coins/-sectors/-pages.xml (per-section indexing reports).
so_what: Owner: submit all four, check Security & Manual actions and Removals are empty.

claim: Original data posts (e.g. which sectors moved most this month) are the most linkable content a data site can produce.
so_what: Next: a monthly sector-performance post built from the sector tables (owner publishes in own words).

claim: Launch venues remove posts that read as generated or break self-promotion rules.
so_what: Owner posts in own words, following each venue's rules (LAUNCH-KIT.md).

claim: Google's link-spam policy names keyword-rich links in distributed widgets and links required by terms of use.
so_what: Widget credit links are brand-only and optional.

claim: On a new domain 'Discovered - currently not indexed' is mostly a demand problem; links from sites Google already crawls create demand.
so_what: Owner: GitHub repo About link/topics, launch posts in own words (LAUNCH-KIT.md), one link a day.

claim: AlternativeTo (DR about 80-82, about 2.1M visits a month) lists apps on the alternatives pages of the tools they replace; free with a slow queue or $5 priority review; new listings' website link is usually nofollow. AI 'alternatives to X' answers draw on such pages.
so_what: Owner: list CryptoPriceTicker.com as a free, privacy-first alternative to CoinMarketCap, CoinGecko and Coinlib (tags: no account, real-time, widgets).

claim: An installable PWA can be listed in the Microsoft Store (PWABuilder + Partner Center) and Google Play (Trusted Web Activity, Digital Asset Links, one-time fee), plus PWA directories and launch sites (Product Hunt, Show HN, DEV #showdev).
so_what: Owner decision: store listings need developer accounts; directories and Show HN cost only time. The manifest and service worker already qualify.

claim: FAQ rich results no longer appear in Google Search (deprecated May 7, 2026); Dataset markup only feeds Dataset Search (Nov 2025); practice problems removed.
so_what: Never add FAQ, HowTo, Dataset or Product markup; keep WebSite, Organization, WebPage/CollectionPage and BreadcrumbList.

claim: Supported and cheap: WebSite, Organization (logo ImageObject, sameAs), WebPage/CollectionPage/WebApplication, BreadcrumbList.
so_what: In place on every page type.

claim: Search Console's Performance report country filter accepts several countries summed into one line (Oct 6, 2026); custom chart annotations exist since Nov 2025; Web search type split into Text-based and Multimodal (Sep 24, 2026).
so_what: Annotate Nov 10 (core update) and Nov 12 (AI Mode model) in Search Console once it has data.

claim: Candidate score = impressions x (site's own expected CTR at that position - current CTR), with at least 100 impressions in 28 days; 'striking distance' alone is folklore (positions 4-10 get 0.5-1.7% of desktop clicks).
so_what: Used by the self-improving loop once telemetry flows.

claim: Cloudflare Web Analytics gives cookieless real-visitor Core Web Vitals.
so_what: Owner: switch it on (STRATEGY D1).

claim: CrUX field data appears only after a site passes Google's popularity threshold.
so_what: D2 (weekly CrUX in the digest) waits for traffic.

claim: Search Console API: rowLimit 25000 with pagination (rows are sorted by clicks, so a low cap drops the rows you want), one finalized day per night, impression-weighted position.
so_what: Implemented in the Apps Script collector.

claim: The site is far below published minimums for SEO split tests (about 1,000 organic visits a day); expect 'inconclusive'. Search Console data lags 2-3 days; titles show effects in days to weeks.
so_what: Judge on impressions and position first; windows of 14 days (titles) and 28 days (content); compare with unchanged coins.

claim: Gary Illyes implied click and query data are not coming to Search Console's AI performance report soon ('nothing to announce'). The report (all sites since Aug 31, 2026) shows AI Overview/AI Mode impressions by page only.
so_what: Judge AI visibility by impressions per page in that report plus GA4 referrals; don't wait for AI click data.

claim: New Search Central page: Google Search sends Referer with the 'origin' policy (https://www.google.com/ or a local Google domain; android-app://com.google.android.googlequicksearchbox/ from the Android app); no query, sometimes blank; analytics won't match Search Console 1:1. Client-side redirects and strict Referrer-Policy on redirects can drop it.
so_what: Our redirects are server-side 301s in _redirects and Referrer-Policy is strict-origin-when-cross-origin on our own responses, which keeps Google's incoming Referer. GA4 counts it as organic; nothing to change.

claim: Reserving space for JavaScript-filled regions (tape, movers, table, charts) took home-page CLS from 0.832 to 0.003.
so_what: Any new JS-filled region needs reserved space in the HTML/CSS.

claim: Restarting flash animations with void el.offsetWidth per cell cost about 570 ms of main thread; alternating two identical keyframes costs nothing.
so_what: Use the two-keyframe trick for any restartable animation.

claim: Dimming the largest element with opacity delayed LCP until the first live tick (2.2 s); muting it by colour gives about 1.0 s.
so_what: Never put opacity on the largest element.

claim: Chrome silently ignored the whole speculation-rules file because of a top-level relative_to; only the console shows it.
so_what: Validate speculation-rules.json by loading a page and reading the console (the crawl lists browser warnings).

claim: Lighthouse's simulated LCP on coin pages (2.7 s) is far above real throttled loads (about 1.0-1.1 s); CrUX field data shows 'not found' until the site passes Google's popularity threshold.
so_what: Trust real measurements and field data over the simulation.

claim: Home page main thread at steady state: about 110-130 ms per second, mostly price-flash paint; JavaScript about 4 ms/s. Worker-thread feeds and opacity-overlay flashes measured worse or no better; rolling digits in the home table raised it to about 320 ms/s.
so_what: Don't move feeds to workers or roll digits in the table; flashes are the feature.

claim: The empty GTM container cost every first visit about 451 KiB and 200 ms of blocking (live home Lighthouse 87); it now loads only after cookie consent. GA4 via gtag.js loads for everyone under Consent Mode v2.
so_what: Owner decision still open: drop GTM entirely or keep it for future tags.

claim: seo-lint budgets (raw bytes): app.js 115 KB, app.css 80 KB, coins.js 25 KB, consent.js 6 KB, flash.js 20 KB, 60 KB HTML per page. As of Nov 16: app.js about 109.5 KB (warning band), app.css about 74.6 KB.
so_what: app.js is the next budget to hit: put new features in their own file (as /race/ did) or trim before adding.

claim: Lighthouse 12.2.1 (mobile, headless Chromium in a cloud session) can produce a one-off outlier: /sector/layer-1/ on a preview scored performance 69 with TBT 1,250 ms once, then 98-99 with TBT 50-160 ms on three re-runs, the same as production (98-100). With PR #18's added text the page has 798 DOM nodes vs 721 live; main-thread work unchanged (~1.3-1.5 s).
so_what: Never act on a single Lighthouse run: run at least three times on both the preview and production and compare medians.

claim: Cloudflare Pages: every branch gets a public preview URL (noindex by default); pages.dev host needed an explicit noindex; free plan 500 builds a month; Workers static assets is recommended for new projects but Pages keeps Early Hints and branch aliases.
so_what: Stay on Pages; the QA flow relies on branch aliases.

claim: This repo is public, so analytics, search queries and personal data must never be committed; a non-AI Apps Script collector writes a sanitized, page-level digest to the private usaflees/cpt-telemetry repo.
so_what: Never add raw telemetry here; the AI never holds credentials or reads raw queries.

claim: Two _dmarc TXT records (p=none and p=reject) void DMARC; www has no DNS record.
so_what: Owner: delete the p=none record; add www as a proxied record with a redirect to the apex.

claim: GitHub guidance (Jul 2026): pin actions to full commit SHAs, job-level permissions, Dependabot.
so_what: Done; Dependabot runs monthly, grouped.

claim: The repo has no LICENSE, so it is source-available, not open source.
so_what: Owner: choose a licence or keep 'public source code' wording; owner also wants the repo private eventually.

claim: Working files (/scripts, /docs, /content, /tests, /.claude, /.github, CLAUDE.md, README, SECURITY.md) are not served: functions/_middleware.js returns 404, limited by _routes.json; check-live verifies.
so_what: Keep _routes.json and the middleware list in sync (seo-lint checks).

claim: GitHub Actions runs a step without an explicit shell as bash -e {0}, without pipefail, so 'cmd | tee' hides a failing cmd; and pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN don't trigger other workflows.
so_what: Workflows here use 'set -o pipefail' before pipes; the data-refresh workflow's push doesn't re-run Site checks, so it runs its own QA and IndexNow.

claim: The domain was re-registered Oct 22, 2026; the earlier site (2021-2022) was the owner's own CodeCanyon PHP crypto price script, so Google's memory of the domain is on-topic. ScamAdviser scores it 0/100 from the old registration.
so_what: Redirect old addresses that match today's pages (needs the owner's 404 export); keep /trust/ factual.

claim: Search Console exports (to Nov 9): only the home page is indexed; every other sitemap URL is 'Discovered - currently not indexed'; Google crawls a handful of URLs a day, mostly re-rendering the home page; about a fifth of requests hit leftovers of the owner's 2021-2022 site on this domain.
so_what: Nothing technical blocks indexing; it's demand. Levers: request indexing for key pages, first links, keep the site cheap to crawl, wait weeks. Hold new URL families.

claim: Google AI Mode answered that CryptoPriceTicker.com 'appears to be offline or defunct' (active about 2018-2022, X @CoinPriceTicker, a Quora space) and recommended Coinlib, Coinpaprika and others (owner's screenshot, 16 Nov). Cause: one indexed page, and no page stated that the site is live, relaunched by the same owner, and privacy-first.
so_what: Fixed on our side 16 Nov (home, /about/#history-h, /trust/, llms.txt, JSON-LD). Owner: request indexing for /, /about/, /trust/; thumbs-down + report the answer with https://cryptopriceticker.com/about/#history-h; update the old X/Quora profiles if they're yours. Re-test the same question.
